title: Why Does Your Stomach GROWL? 🤫
description:
Your stomach picks the quietest room to growl... and it isn't just complaining. A couple of hours after a meal, your gut starts cleaning: a wave of muscle squeezes all the way through, sweeping out leftovers and bacteria. With no food inside to muffle it, it's just gas and juice squeezed through a tube. It even has a name: borborygmi. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Full stomach? The same squeezes happen; the food just muffles them. And in 1912 a student swallowed a balloon so his professor could record his stomach: his hunger pangs lined up with the squeezes.
